title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:
This consolidated standards document defines the recommended patterns and mandatory requirements for API design, coding practices, infrastructure IaC, model-serving, observability, performance targets, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process across Redwood Inference. The goal is to ensure predictable behavior, operational reliability, and consistent developer ergonomics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Audience and ownership:
- Primary audience: engineering teams (platform, runtime, infra, API), product architects, SREs.
- Document owner: engineering (Architecture & Standards guild).
- Review cadence: quarterly reviews and after any major infra or product release.

1) API standards
Purpose: provide a consistent, versionable, observable surface for all external and internal APIs (REST and gRPC).
Key requirements:
- Versioning: use semantic versioning in the URL or API gateway header. For REST endpoints use /v{MAJOR}/... for breaking changes.
- OpenAPI: every HTTP API must provide an OpenAPI 3.0 (or newer) spec stored in the service repo under /api/openapi.yaml and published to the API catalog.
- Authentication: use JWT-based service tokens for internal services and API keys / OAuth for external customers. Never accept unauthenticated traffic.
- Rate limiting headers: APIs must return X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset for externally facing endpoints.
- Error model: standardize on Problem Details for HTTP APIs (RFC 7807). Error responses must include code, message, retriable boolean, and correlation_id. Example:

  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Content-Type: application/problem+json
  {
    "type": "https://api.redwood.ai/errors/rate_limited",
    "title": "Rate limit exceeded",
    "status": 429,
    "detail": "Request rate 120rpm exceeds limit 100rpm",
    "instance": "/requests/abc123",
    "retriable": true,
    "correlation_id": "req-20260220-xyz"
  }

- Idempotency & retry: state-changing endpoints must accept an Idempotency-Key header with a 24-CHAR hex token. Retry guidance documented in client SDKs.
- Telemetry hooks: every API handler must emit the following metrics: request_count, request_success_count, request_error_count (by code), p50/p95 latency, and guest_user_rate. Logs must include correlation_id and request metadata.
- API contract changes: follow the Contract-First workflow — update OpenAPI, run contract tests (consumer-driven tests), then roll out. Deprecation window for breaking changes: 90 days for external, 14 days for internal services unless pre-approved by product.

2) Coding standards
Purpose: maintain readability, testability, and low cognitive load in codebases.
Language and tooling guidelines:
- Primary languages: Go (backend infra & runtimes), Python (data, evals, SDKs), TypeScript (console, SDKs). Use the language-native linters and formatters.
- Formatting & linting: enforce gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/flake8 for Python, and prettier/eslint for TypeScript.
- Commit & PR rules:
  1. Commit message format: <scope>: <short summary>
     - Example: api: add v2 /models endpoint
  2. PR size: prefer < 500 lines changed; > 500 requires architectural review.
  3. Require 2 approvers for changes to core infra/runtime code.
- Testing: minimum unit test coverage 70% for service-level packages. Critical runtime components (scheduler, kernel selector) must have >=85% coverage and fuzz/chaos tests.
- Secrets: never commit secrets to git; use Vault/KMS for secrets. Pre-commit hooks should block accidental high-entropy strings.
- Code owners: CODEOWNERS must be present and kept current.

3) Infrastructure (IaC) standards
Purpose: ensure repeatable, auditable infra environments across environments (dev/staging/prod).
- Primary IaC: Terraform (>=1.3). Modules must be namespaced as: tf-<team>-<component> and published to the private module registry.
- Environments: canonical environments are dev, staging, prod. Each environment must be in a separate AWS account (or cloud project) and have unique VPCs.
- Tagging & cost allocation: every provisioned resource must include tags: owner, team, environment, project, cost-center.
- Secrets & keys: use KMS/HSM for key storage and AWS Secrets Manager / Vault for application secrets. Rotations: keys rotated at least annually; service credentials rotated on role change.
- CI gating: terraform plan must run in CI; apply only from a restricted pipeline with at least 2 reviewers for prod changes.
- Rollback: IaC changes must include roll-forward and rollback plans, with automated safety checks for destructive actions (e.g., replacing an RDS instance).

4) Model-serving standards
Purpose: safe, reliable, and performant model deployments across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.
- Model catalog & metadata: every model must have a catalog entry (catalog.yaml) including: model_id, architecture, family, size, quantization_profile (if any), max_sequence_length, recommended_batch_size, owner, and evaluation badges. Store catalog in /models/catalog.
- Versioning: model binaries and configs must be versioned. Model_id:v{MAJOR.MINOR}. Rollouts tie API model_version to catalog versions.
- Quantization profiles: define and store quantization profiles in /models/quantization-profiles with fields: dtype, int8_per_layer (yes/no), suggested kernels.
- Compatibility matrix: maintain a matrix mapping model families to runtime kernel support (e.g., "llama2-70b": [cuda-kernel-v3, aten-opset-2]).
- Deployments & rollouts:
  1. Canary: 5% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor errors and latency.
  2. Ramp: 25% for 1 hour, 50% for 2 hours, 100% after 6 hours if health metrics OK.
  3. Auto-rollback: if error_rate > 0.5% (absolute) or p95 latency regresses > 30% relative to baseline for two consecutive windows (5m), trigger rollback.
- Autoscaling & batching: define target GPU utilization 60-75% for cost-efficiency. Use continuous batching with a max_batch_size and latency SLOs per model class. Example config (YAML snippet):

  model_deployment:
    model_id: "llama2-13b:v1"
    max_batch_size: 128
    preferred_batch_latency_ms: 80
    min_replicas: 2
    max_replicas: 50

- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for prompt-heavy workloads. Cache hit rate target > 60% for prompt-optimized workloads.

5) Observability standards
Purpose: enable fast incident diagnosis and capacity planning.
- Metrics (mandatory):
  - api.request_count (by route, method, model_id)
  - api.request_success_count, api.request_error_count (by error_code)
  - api.latency_ms_p50/p95/p99 (by route and model_class)
  - runtime.gpu_utilization, runtime.vram_free_mb, runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio
  - infra.node_cpu_util, infra.disk_iops, infra.network_tx_bytes
- Tracing: use OpenTelemetry. Every externally-facing request must start a trace with service, route, model_id, and correlation_id tags. Spans must be emitted for scheduling, kernel selection, token-generation loop, and external calls (e.g., embeddings service).
- Logs: structured JSON with fields: timestamp, level, service, host, correlation_id, model_id, request_id, message, attrs. Sensitive fields must be redacted before indexing.
- Dashboards & alerts:
  - Per-model dashboard: p95 latency, error rate, throughput, batch size distribution, KV cache hit.
  - Alerting thresholds (default):
    * page if error_rate > 1% for 2 consecutive 5m windows or p95 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 10m.
    * notify Slack on-call if GPU host unresponsive for 3 minutes.
- Retention: high-cardinality logs (debug) retained 7 days, structured request traces 30 days, aggregated metrics 13 months (prometheus+long-term store).

6) Performance standards & SLOs
Purpose: clear performance and reliability targets for product and infra teams. SLO taxonomy: service_class = small_model, mid_model, large_model (based on model parameters).
- Target SLOs (hosted API default):
  - small_model (<=8B): availability 99.95% monthly, p95 first-token latency <= 150ms, p99 <= 400ms.
  - mid_model (8B-70B): availability 99.9% monthly, p95 first-token latency <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms.
  - large_model (>70B): availability 99.8% monthly, p95 first-token latency <= 900ms, p99 <= 2000ms.
- Throughput & batching guidance:
  - Prefer dynamic batching with target latency SLOs; configure preferred_batch_latency_ms per model.
  - If batch_size > 64 and p95 latency exceeds SLO, reduce max_batch_size or scale replicas.
- Cost-performance guardrails: use quantization when quality regression < 1% on eval prompt set and cost reduction > 25%. Document quantization profile and A/B evaluation results.
- Benchmarks: every model onboarded must include: cold-start 95th latency, warm steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), memory footprint, and deterministic kernel path for the canonical sequence lengths. Store benchmark results in /perf/benchmarks/<model_id>.json.

7) Decision records (ADRs) process
Purpose: capture and communicate architecture decisions with context, status, and owners.
- Template (must be used for all medium+ impact decisions):
  - Title
  - Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded
  - Context: background and constraints
  - Decision: chosen approach and trade-offs
  - Consequences: operational and technical impacts
  - Date and authors
  - Related ADRs and links
- Storage: ADRs live in the service repo under /docs/adrs and are mirrored to Confluence. Filename format: yyyy-mm-dd-brief-title.md.
- When to create an ADR:
  - Any decision that affects cross-team contracts, infra topology, security posture, or performance characteristics.
  - If the change requires one-week+ rollout planning or migration scripts.
- Review and approval: ADRs affecting multiple teams require reviewers from impacted teams and an approver from Architecture guild.
- Example ADR summary entries (must be included in release notes for major changes):
  - ADR-2025-09-11: Standardize API error model to RFC7807 (accepted) — rationale and migration plan.
  - ADR-2026-01-20: Adopt Terraform module namespace tf-<team>-<component> (accepted) — policy and enforcement.
  - ADR-2026-02-14: Use quantized INT8 inference by default for small models (proposed) — evaluation checklist included.

8) Governance & enforcement
- Mandatory vs recommended: fields and SLOs prefixed with MUST are mandatory. Teams will be audited quarterly. Recommendations are labeled SHOULD.
- Exceptions: request via architecture-exceptions RFC and store exception record in /policies/exception-log with owner and expiry. Exceptions for prod require engineering leadership sign-off.
- Compliance checks: CI/CD pipelines must run linters, contract tests, terraform plan, and a lightweight perf smoke test for runtime changes.

9) Onboarding and templates
- Repo templates: service template (Go), model deployment template (YAML), ADR template, OpenAPI stub.
- Quickstart: see /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates for step-by-step onboarding to publish an OpenAPI, create a model catalog entry, and register metrics.

10) Appendices
A. Example ADR header (Markdown):

  # ADR: Standardize API Error Model to RFC7807
  - Status: accepted
  - Date: 2025-09-11
  - Authors: Ava Martinez, James Chen
  ## Context
  (background...)
  ## Decision
  (decision...)
  ## Consequences
  (impacts...)

B. Example monitoring thresholds (text table):

  Metric | Warning threshold | Page threshold
  -------|-------------------|----------------
  api.p95_latency | > 0.9 * SLO for 10m | > 1.5 * SLO for 10m
  api.error_rate | > 0.5% for 10m | > 1% for 10m
  runtime.gpu_util | > 85% sustained for 15m | > 95% sustained for 10m

C. Quick checklist to onboard a new model (numbered):
  1. Create catalog.yaml with metadata and owner.
  2. Add benchmark JSON to /perf/benchmarks.
  3. Add OpenAPI contract update if new endpoint is exposed.
  4. Run contract tests and performance smoke tests in CI.
  5. Deploy to canary and monitor for 6h before ramp.

D. Contacts and ownership:
- Architecture guild: architecture@redwood.ai (Primary contact for ADRs and exceptions).
- SRE on-call: see /oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks for roster.
- Model on-boarding owner: Maya Patel (maya.p@redwood.ai).
